code.title: Print Numbers from 1 to N
code.description:
A gallery exhibit features a number column that lights up from 1 to N. Read N and print every integer from 1 to N, one per line.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: N.

Output Format:
N lines, containing the numbers 1, 2, 3, ..., N in order, one number per line.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000

code.title: Natural Number Sum with for Loop
code.description:
A warehouse robot stacks crates: level 1 holds 1 crate, level 2 holds 2 crates, and so on up to level N. Read N and print the total number of crates in the stack (1 + 2 + ... + N), computed with a loop.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: N.

Output Format:
Sum of 1 to <N>: <total>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 10000

code.title: Multiplication Table of N
code.description:
A math tutor app draws the multiplication table of a number. Read N and print its table from N x 1 up to N x 10, one line per product.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: N.

Output Format:
10 lines of the form <N> x <i> = <product> for i from 1 to 10.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 20

code.title: Sum of Even Numbers up to N
code.description:
A stadium LED ribbon flashes every even seat number before a match. Read N and print the sum of all even numbers from 1 up to N (2 + 4 + 6 + ...), computed with a while loop.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: N.

Output Format:
Even sum up to <N>: <sum>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 10000

code.title: Count Digits of a Number
code.description:
A bank teller verifies account numbers by counting their digits. Read a non-negative integer and print how many digits it has. Use a do-while loop so that 0 is correctly counted as 1 digit.

Input Format:
One line with one non-negative integer.

Output Format:
Digits: <count>

Constraints:
0 <= number <= 2000000000

code.title: Reverse the Digits of a Number
code.description:
A mirror-lock app unlocks when the user types the reverse of a code number. Read a non-negative integer and print its digits reversed as a number (reversing 1200 gives 21 because leading zeros disappear).

Input Format:
One line with one non-negative integer.

Output Format:
Reversed: <reversed number>

Constraints:
0 <= number <= 2000000000

code.title: Daily Calorie Target Tracker
code.description:
A fitness app tracks calories against a daily target. Read the number of days N and the calorie target T, then the calories eaten on each day. Print the cumulative total after every day, then the total consumed and whether the target was reached.

Input Format:
First token: N (number of days). Second token: the target T. Then N integers: calories consumed each day.

Output Format:
Day <i>: <cumulative total> (one line per day)
Total consumed: <sum>
Target: <T>
Status: Target met (when the total is at least T) or Status: Below target

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 31, 0 <= each calorie value <= 5000, 0 <= T <= 200000

Day <i>: <steps> (total <running total>) (one line per day)

Best day: <day> (<best count> steps)

code.title: Factorial and Trailing Zeros
code.description:
A puzzle factory stamps gift boxes with every distinct arrangement of N items, which is N factorial. The quality team also records how many trailing zeros appear on the printed label. Read N, compute N! with a loop, then count its trailing zeros by repeatedly dividing by 10 while the last digit is 0.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: N.

Output Format:
Factorial: <N factorial>
Trailing zeros: <count>

Constraints:
0 <= N <= 12 (0! is 1 and has no trailing zeros)

code.title: Prime Keys in a Range
code.description:
A cybersecurity trainer generates prime demo keys. Read a range A to B inclusive and print every prime in it in ascending order on one line, then the count. Each number is tested by trying divisors d while d * d is at most the number.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: A and B.

Output Format:
Primes: <p1> <p2> ... <pk> (print none when the range has no primes)
Count: <k>

Constraints:
1 <= A <= B <= 500

code.title: Digit Sum and Product Machine
code.description:
A bank card validator inspects account numbers. Read a non-negative integer and compute the sum of its digits and the product of its digits with a do-while loop, so the number 0 is processed as the single digit 0 (sum 0 and product 0).

Input Format:
One line with one non-negative integer.

Output Format:
Digit sum: <sum>
Digit product: <product>

Constraints:
0 <= number <= 2000000000

code.title: ATM Transaction Session
code.description:
An ATM processes a session of withdrawal requests. The log starts with N (the number of records) and a starting balance B, followed by N record amounts processed in order with a do-while loop. An amount within the current balance is approved and deducted; anything larger is declined. A record equal to -1 means the session was cancelled: print the cancellation line and stop processing immediately, ignoring any remaining records.

Input Format:
First token: N. Second token: starting balance B. Then N integers, each an amount between 0 and 100000 or the cancel marker -1.

Output Format:
One line per processed record: TXN <i>: Approved, balance <new balance> or TXN <i>: Declined
When cancelled: Cancelled at record <i>
Processed: <number of records actually processed>
Final balance: <balance>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 50, 0 <= B <= 100000

code.title: Fibonacci Series Printer
code.description:
A beekeeper models colony growth with the Fibonacci sequence 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, ... where every term is the sum of the two before it. Read K and print the first K terms on one line separated by single spaces, then how many terms were printed.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: K.

Output Format:
The first K Fibonacci terms separated by single spaces
Terms: <K>

Constraints:
1 <= K <= 30

code.title: Battery Drain Cycle Counter
code.description:
A drone battery simulator drains charge in fixed steps. The battery starts at P percent and loses R percent every cycle, never going below 0, and each cycle prints the remaining charge. One line with three integers: P (start percent), R (drain per cycle) and T (cutoff threshold).

Output Format:
One line per cycle: Cycle <i>: <remaining>%
Cycles used: <count>
Final charge: <remaining>%

Constraints:
0 <= T < P <= 100, 1 <= R <= 100

code.title: Vending Machine Change Dispenser
code.description:
A vending machine dispenses change using the denominations 500, 100, 50, 10, 5 and 1, always taking as many of the largest denomination as possible before moving to the next one. The day log starts with N (the maximum number of customers) followed by one refund amount per customer, and the very last token of the log is -1. For every customer the machine prints its denomination breakdown, and at the end of the day it prints the accumulated totals per denomination. Processing stops after N customers or at the -1 marker, whichever comes first.

Input Format:
First token: N. Then the refund amounts (one per customer), with the final token -1 marking the end of the log.

Output Format:
For each customer:
Customer <i>: <amount>
  500 x <a>, 100 x <b>, 50 x <c>, 10 x <d>, 5 x <e>, 1 x <f>
After all customers:
Denomination totals:
500: <total>
100: <total>
50: <total>
10: <total>
5: <total>
1: <total>
Customers served: <count>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 20, 1 <= amount <= 5000, the log always ends with -1

code.title: Delivery Route Analyzer
code.description:
A courier company reviews its delivery routes. The input gives D (days) and S (stops per day), then D groups of S integers: kilometres covered at each stop. For each day print the day total and its longest stop (earliest stop wins a tie). After all days print the grand total, the average per day with two decimals, and the busiest day (largest day total; earliest day wins a tie).

Input Format:
One line with two integers: D and S. Then D x S integers: stop distances in km, day by day.

Output Format:
Day <i>: total <T> km, longest stop <j> (<max> km) (one line per day)
Total distance: <grand total> km
Average per day: <average with 2 decimals> km
Busiest day: <day> (<max total> km)

Constraints:
1 <= D <= 10, 1 <= S <= 20, 0 <= each stop <= 500

code.description:
A tournament desk types player scores into a scoreboard and finishes the list by typing the sentinel -1 (real scores are between 0 and 100, so -1 can never be a score). A sequence of integers (0 to 100 each) terminated by -1. At least one score appears before the sentinel.

Output Format:
Players: <count>
Highest: <max>
Lowest: <min>
Average: <average with 2 decimals>
Above average: <count>

Constraints:
1 <= number of scores <= 1000, 0 <= score <= 100, the input always ends with -1

Output Format:
One line per digit: Digit <d>: <letters> letters (for 0 and 1: Digit <d>: no letters)
Total letter combinations: <product>

1 <= length of passcode <= 10, every character is a digit 0 to 9
